scientific_hypothesis: A periodic Si/SiO2 quarter-wave stack with 10 layer pairs can achieve simultaneous high transmittance at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm while maintaining stopbands at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm through natural Bragg reflection harmonics.
expected_advantages: Fewer layers needed due to high Δn
Natural harmonic transmission windows may align with dual passbands
known_risks: Quarter-wave design may not precisely align both passbands simultaneously
Stopband edges may not match required 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm exactly
Si absorption in mid-IR may reduce peak transmittance
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise as layer thicknesses converge to quarter-wave condition at geometric mean wavelength
tightest_margin should remain positive if stopband rejection exceeds passband leakage
valid_candidates count should stay high since Si/SiO2 are low-loss dielectrics in mid-IR
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 5 for three consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 20% and continue
